content:
As of 2025, artificial intelligence has moved beyond the category of standalone applications to become a foundational technology layer integrated into the business world and public sector processes. Below are the 10 key verticals that stand out during this period, in which autonomous agents are gaining operational capabilities, video production is accelerating, and corporate efficiency is being redefined.

1. Autonomous AI Agents

Chatbots alone have been replaced by autonomous agents capable of planning and completing end-to-end tasks via API connections. These systems, which are becoming widespread in 2025 for customer service, sales assistance, and IT support requests, have gained browser-based processing capabilities thanks to OpenAI’s “Operator” initiative. According to IBM surveys, 99 percent of developers are working on agent technologies.

2. Enterprise Artificial Intelligence

Companies have focused on cross-departmental scaling by processing their own data with generative AI. According to McKinsey data, 88 percent of companies are using AI in at least one business unit. A Menlo Ventures report shows that enterprise generative AI revenue will reach $37 billion by 2025 and that the rate of adoption into production is higher compared to traditional software.

3. AI-Powered Video Production

Text-to-video generation and automated editing tools have accelerated marketing and content production processes. Nearly half of marketers have incorporated these tools into their daily workflows. Large-scale partnerships in the sector, such as the $1 billion licensing agreement between Disney and OpenAI, are drawing attention.

4. Health Technologies (HealthTech)

The use of AI in medical image analysis, clinical documentation, and drug discovery is becoming standard. The FDA has approved more than 500 AI-based medical devices as of the end of 2025. According to NVIDIA reports, 81 percent of healthcare organizations reported an increase in revenue following AI investments.

5. Finance and Fintech

In the banking and finance sector, fraud detection, risk scoring, and algorithmic trading are taking center stage. 79 percent of major U.S. banks have integrated generative AI into their operations. Payment giants like Visa are blocking billions of dollars in suspicious transactions using AI-powered filters.

6. Defense Industry

The use of AI is on the rise in the areas of intelligence analysis, autonomous unmanned systems, and cyber defense. The U.S. Department of Defense and NATO are expanding their budgets for decision-support systems and autonomous projects. Target detection using computer vision and war simulations are at the heart of modern defense strategies.

7. Legal Technology (LegalTech)

Contract review, case law search, and document summarization are being accelerated by artificial intelligence. Seventy-two percent of legal professionals use these tools on a weekly basis. Major law firms are leveraging tools such as Harvey and Lexis+ AI for risk analysis and drafting processes.

8. AI-Powered SaaS

AI assistants embedded in CRM, project management, and office software have become standard. 67 percent of SaaS companies offer AI features in their products. A significant portion of corporate spending is directed toward these smart features integrated into existing workflows.

9. Vibe Coding

In software development, natural language-based code generation and management (vibe coding) is emerging as a new approach that boosts productivity. According to Stack Overflow data, 84% of developers use AI tools. Tools like Copilot and Cursor shorten development times by bringing code completion and refactoring capabilities directly into the IDE.

10. Marketing and Content Creation

Personalization, targeting, and media optimization have become algorithmic. 93 percent of marketers use AI to accelerate content creation, while 90 percent use it to speed up decision-making processes. Meta and Google’s advertising tools automate the creation of creative variations and budget allocation.
